title: Add session-scoped chat history and multi-round tool conversation support
objective: Add a session-scoped chat API that accumulates user, assistant, and tool messages, replays complete provider history across additional tool rounds, supports configurable user-message interruption while tools run, preserves the initial task and taskSchema separately from provider messages, and documents and validates the XML prompt and HTTP projection contracts.

branch.name: wi-0009-chat-session-history
branch.rationale: The repository workflow processes this scoped feature as an ordered set of commits on the current branch; the intended work boundary is recorded without requiring a topic branch.

request.text: Create a new chat-session architecture for the llm package. Expose chatFactory.createSession with session-scoped AbortSignal and an EventSink compatible with DebugEvents/DebugSink, add LlmChatSession history semantics, preserve task and taskSchema separately from public LlmRequest.messages and raw ProviderCompletionRequest.messages, replay complete assistant/tool message history across multiple tool rounds, support additional user messages with configurable interruption while tools run, add provider HTTP projection documentation and a discoverable projection class, add and validate schemas/prompt/v1/llm-prompt.xsd, provide three executable chat samples, document the non-concurrency assumption, exclude compaction and checkpointing, and prepare a work item with an initial design task whose outputs and verification obligations cover all requirements.

scope.name: chat-factory-and-session-api
scope.description: Expose a public chatFactory with createSession and an LlmChatSession instance boundary for each independent conversation.
scope.reason: The public API should make session ownership explicit and prevent callers from treating one mutable conversation as a global provider.

scope.name: session-options-and-lifecycle
scope.description: Define ChatFactoryCreateSessionOptions including AbortSignal, an EventSink compatible with the repository DebugSink/DebugEvent pattern, provider-layer pass-through options, and UserMessageInterruptsToolRound with a default of false.
scope.reason: Session-scoped cancellation, observability, and user-message behavior must be configured when the session is created.

scope.name: provider-message-history
scope.description: Keep task and taskSchema as distinct completion-request context fields while adding public LlmRequest.messages and raw ProviderCompletionRequest.messages for accumulated user, assistant, and tool messages.
scope.reason: The initial task context must remain available while the provider receives a canonical replayable conversation history.

scope.name: multi-round-tool-replay
scope.description: Append assistant tool-call messages and matching tool result messages to session history and send the complete ordered history on every subsequent provider request.
scope.reason: Additional rounds must preserve call-round-1 and call-round-2, not send only the latest tool result.

scope.name: additional-user-message-semantics
scope.description: Support additional user messages in an active session and specify whether they interrupt a tool round or wait until a long-running tool round completes.
scope.reason: Chat behavior requires back-and-forth user/model turns as well as an explicit policy for messages arriving while tools are running.

scope.name: provider-http-projection
scope.description: Document the mapping from normalized request fields, prompt XML, session messages, tools, credentials, and reasoning settings to the OpenRouter Chat Completions HTTP request, and place the mapping in a discoverable projection class/module.
scope.reason: The transport contract must be inspectable and testable rather than hidden inside the provider method.

scope.name: prompt-xml-schema
scope.description: Add an XML Schema under schemas/prompt/v1/llm-prompt.xsd for the XML prompt emitted in the initial user message, with descriptions and schema-validation evidence.
scope.reason: The generated prompt XML is a contract and needs a durable, validated schema definition.

scope.name: executable-chat-samples
scope.description: Add executable provider-free samples for ordinary back-and-forth chat, interruptible long-running tool calls, and blocked user messages during a long-running tool call.
scope.reason: The session behavior must be documented through runnable examples, including both configured tool-round policies.

scope.name: concurrency-documentation
scope.description: Document that callers of LlmChatSession must enforce the non-concurrency assumption and that the session does not implement concurrent mutation, compaction, or checkpointing.
scope.reason: The requested first implementation has a deliberately narrow lifecycle boundary and must state its operational assumptions.

scope.name: verification-and-handoff
scope.description: Define deterministic tests, schema validation, sample discovery, typecheck, build, projection inspection, and changed-path review sufficient to hand the design to implementation.
scope.reason: The feature crosses public types, session state, provider transport, XML schema, documentation, and executable samples.

nonGoals.name: compaction
nonGoals.description: Do not implement context compaction, summarization, truncation, token budgeting, or history reduction.
nonGoals.reason: This phase accumulates and replays session messages without reducing history.

nonGoals.name: checkpointing
nonGoals.description: Do not implement checkpoint persistence, session restore, durable history stores, or checkpoint concepts in the public API.
nonGoals.reason: Checkpointing is explicitly deferred and must not shape the initial session contract.

nonGoals.name: implicit-session-concurrency
nonGoals.description: Do not add a mutex, queue, optimistic concurrency protocol, or other automatic concurrent-mutation mechanism to LlmChatSession.
nonGoals.reason: Callers are responsible for enforcing the documented non-concurrency assumption at the session boundary.

nonGoals.name: live-provider-and-real-side-effects
nonGoals.description: Do not require live OpenRouter credentials or real external tool side effects for tests and samples.
nonGoals.reason: The repository uses deterministic provider and tool doubles for local evidence.

nonGoals.name: historical-git-rewrite
nonGoals.description: Do not rewrite, reset, amend, or force-push existing Git history.
nonGoals.reason: The feature must be delivered as new commits on top of the recorded baseline.

items.name: session-factory-api
items.description: The public package exposes chatFactory.createSession as the factory-backed LlmChatProvider/session boundary and returns an independent LlmChatSession instance for each call.
items.reason: A factory makes the per-chat lifecycle and ownership boundary explicit.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Public source exports and generated declarations expose chatFactory, createSession, ChatFactoryCreateSessionOptions, and LlmChatSession with a documented per-session ownership model.
Two sessions created from the factory have independent message histories, options, cancellation state, and debug sinks.

items.name: session-options
items.description: createSession accepts an AbortSignal, an EventSink compatible with DebugEvents/DebugSink, provider-layer pass-through configuration, and UserMessageInterruptsToolRound defaulting to false.
items.reason: Session-level control and observability must flow to all provider and tool activity without requiring repeated per-turn wiring.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The option type and implementation define the AbortSignal and EventSink/DebugEvent sink ownership, identify any additional provider pass-through options, and default UserMessageInterruptsToolRound to false.
Cancellation and debug events from a session-created completion reach the provider/tool orchestration layers with credentials and secret values excluded from diagnostics.

items.name: task-and-message-separation
items.description: Completion requests retain task and taskSchema as separate context fields, expose LlmRequest.messages at the public/session boundary, and add ProviderCompletionRequest.messages as the ordered raw-provider conversation history.
items.reason: The initial objectives, rules, task schema, and relevant files remain distinct from subsequent chat messages.

acceptanceCriteria.description: TypeScript types, normalization, and provider requests retain task and taskSchema separately while exposing LlmRequest.messages and ProviderCompletionRequest.messages without embedding tool results into the initial XML prompt.

The initial user message contains the documented XML prompt context, while system instructions, assistant messages, tool messages, and later user messages have distinct provider-neutral message roles.

items.name: complete-tool-history-replay
items.description: Every automatic tool round appends the model assistant message containing tool calls and the matching tool result messages, and every later provider request sends the complete ordered session history.
items.reason: The model must receive call-round-1 and call-round-2 context in the request that follows the second round.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A deterministic two-round test proves request 2 includes the first assistant tool-call message and its tool results, and request 3 includes both assistant tool-call messages and both rounds of tool results in valid order.

OpenRouter projection emits assistant tool_calls before matching role=tool messages, preserves tool_call_id correlation, supports parallel calls, and retains the full history across terminal completion.

items.name: additional-user-messages
items.description: LlmChatSession supports additional user messages after and between model turns without discarding prior history.
items.reason: The package must support back-and-forth chat rather than only one initial task followed by an internal tool loop.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A deterministic chat test proves a later user message is appended after the prior assistant response and the next provider request contains the complete preceding conversation followed by the new user message.

The design and implementation define how a user message is accepted, rejected, queued, or surfaced while a tool round is active without inserting it between an assistant tool-call message and its required tool results.

items.name: interruptible-tool-rounds
items.description: UserMessageInterruptsToolRound controls whether an additional user message can interrupt a running tool round; false is the default and both interruptible and blocked behavior are defined.
items.reason: The requested samples require one session that accepts an interrupt while a long-running tool continues and another that blocks the user message.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Interrupt-enabled behavior is deterministic: the additional user message receives a model response while pending tool work remains observable and safely completes or is cancelled according to the documented lifecycle.

Default blocked behavior is deterministic: a user message submitted during a long-running tool call does not enter model history until the configured tool round completes, and the behavior is documented.

items.name: http-projection-boundary
items.description: The provider HTTP projection is implemented in a discoverable dedicated class/module and documented next to the request schema.
items.reason: The mapping from package contracts to OpenRouter wire messages must be explicit, independently testable, and easy to find.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The projection documentation maps task, taskSchema, messages, system instructions, files, tools, model, thinking, credentials, tool_call_id, and assistant tool_calls to their OpenRouter HTTP destinations and identifies fields that remain local-only.

Focused provider tests inspect serialized HTTP bodies and prove that full session message history, assistant tool calls, tool results, and tool definitions are projected correctly without leaking credentials.

items.name: prompt-xml-schema
items.description: The repository contains schemas/prompt/v1/llm-prompt.xsd describing the XML structure emitted in the initial user message, with element and attribute descriptions.
items.reason: The XML prompt is a stable contract and must be validated independently of the JSON request contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The XSD describes llmPrompt versioning, task content and attributes, optional taskSchema, files/file attributes and content encoding, and optional outputSchema with human-readable documentation annotations.
The XML schema and representative generated prompt fixtures pass schema-validate or the repository-approved XML schema validation command, with the exact validation command recorded.

items.name: chat-samples
items.description: The samples directory includes three executable provider-free chat examples: ordinary back-and-forth, interruptible long-running tools, and blocked user input during a long-running tool.
items.reason: Runnable examples are required to document session behavior and the two user-message policies.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The ordinary chat sample demonstrates at least one user/model back-and-forth exchange and emits the repository-standard single JSON result envelope.
The interruptible-tool sample demonstrates a long-running tool, an additional user message, a model response while the tool remains pending, and captured history/events proving the behavior.
The blocked-tool sample uses a bounded approximately three-second tool, demonstrates the default blocked user-message behavior, and emits assertions proving the message was not processed early.

items.name: non-concurrency-and-scope-documentation
items.description: Public documentation states that LlmChatSession callers must enforce the non-concurrency assumption, while compaction and checkpointing are explicit non-goals.
items.reason: The initial session boundary intentionally avoids automatic concurrent mutation and persistence complexity.

acceptanceCriteria.description: LlmChatSession documentation states that callers must not concurrently mutate or submit turns to one session and identifies the behavior if the assumption is violated.
Documentation and tests contain no checkpointing or compaction implementation, public API, or implied behavior; session history simply accumulates and is sent to the provider.

items.name: typescript-conventions-and-gates
items.description: The implementation follows the repository TypeScript, native ESM, formatting, naming, testing, and validation conventions.
items.reason: The work changes public TypeScript contracts and must remain consistent with the existing package and generated declarations.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The design and implementation use strict TypeScript, explicit .js ESM imports, readonly public contract fields, existing error vocabulary, existing DebugEvent/DebugSink patterns, and no unconfirmed dependencies.
npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build, sample discovery, schema validation, git diff --check, conflict-marker scan, generated declaration inspection, and changed-path review all pass.
